technologies: PyPA pyproject.toml, Dependency Groups, and pylock.toml specifications
baseline.versionPolicy: Stable outcomes apply across versions; recheck mechanisms and defaults against the supported interpreter and packaging tools.

hardOutcomes: Declared pure cores do not reverse-depend on framework or vendor runtime types.
Imports are acyclic and do not depend on partial initialization order.
State, side effects, and lifecycle-bearing resources have explicit owners.

invariants.outcome: Import dependencies are acyclic, declared pure cores do not depend on framework or vendor runtime types, adopted protocol, storage, and vendor types are translated or proven stable and non-leaking at their declared boundaries, and every authoritative fact, shared mutable state, and long-lived task has an explicit owner or conflict protocol.
invariants.equivalenceCriteria: Flat modules, framework-shaped applications, and layered packages all qualify when repeatable dependency evidence, boundary translations, and ownership paths prove the same result without requiring an unused Domain layer.

invariants.outcome: Configuration, connections, transactions, files, tasks, threads, processes, and workers have bounded startup, cancellation, shutdown, and cleanup semantics.
invariants.equivalenceCriteria: Framework hooks, context managers, explicit composition roots, or other mechanisms qualify when ownership and every failure path are observable and bounded.

invariants.outcome: Untrusted inputs receive runtime validation and protected resources receive actor, tenant, scope, and ownership authorization without leaking secrets through artifacts or observability.
invariants.equivalenceCriteria: Different validation, authorization, and secret-injection tools comply when negative tests and artifact inspection protect the same boundaries.

invariants.outcome: Timeout, cancellation, retry, duplicate delivery, transaction, migration, cache, and external-side-effect behavior follows the real failure semantics of each adopted capability.
invariants.equivalenceCriteria: An alternative control is valid when it bounds work, preserves required consistency, and proves safe duplicate and partial-failure behavior.

invariants.outcome: Every declared Library, CLI, Service, and Worker entry and deliverable is identifiable and reproducibly validated from a clean checkout with consistent distribution, import package, public API, requires-python, dependency, tool, generated-input, Python-version, and platform contracts.
invariants.equivalenceCriteria: A non-distributed source application complies when clean source-entry evidence exercises its actual runtime contract; a distributed project additionally requires clean installed-artifact evidence that binds metadata, public API, entry points, package data, and the declared Python and platform matrix.

invariants.outcome: Process creation and worker sizing match the supported platform start method and do not inherit unsafe pools, sockets, locks, threads, or random state.
invariants.equivalenceCriteria: Spawn, forkserver, safe post-fork recreation, or another verified process model qualifies when platform tests prove resource isolation and bounded capacity.

proves: Selected source files compile as Python syntax.
doesNotProve: Imports are side-effect safe or delivered package contents are complete.

proves: The repository-selected test runner passes the exercised behaviors.
doesNotProve: Untested platforms, entry points, and failure paths are correct.

proves: The declared build backend can create distribution artifacts.
doesNotProve: A clean installation contains every required module and data file.

scenarios.failure: Source-level tests pass while an actual Library import, CLI exit path, Service lifecycle, or Worker retry and drain contract is missing or points at different code.
scenarios.requiredOutcome: Exercise every declared entry through its real public or process boundary, including applicable startup, input, output, readiness, interruption, retry, drain, and shutdown behavior.

scenarios.failure: Editable or source-root tests pass while the built wheel omits modules, data, typing markers, or entry points.
scenarios.requiredOutcome: Install and smoke-test the normal artifact in a clean environment; also test the sdist-to-wheel route when an sdist is shipped.

scenarios.failure: A platform start-method change or fork after threads duplicates unsafe resources and corrupts lifecycle assumptions.
scenarios.requiredOutcome: Pin or discover the real start method, recreate unsafe resources after process creation, and validate declared platform and worker combinations.

scenarios.failure: Metadata or documentation claims a Python version or platform that cannot import, run the declared entry, or pass the risk-relevant tests.
scenarios.requiredOutcome: Run the actual entry and risk-relevant tests on every declared stable Python and critical platform combination, including the minimum version, and keep requires-python and artifact tags consistent with the evidence.
